To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
laminin is a substrate that promotes neurite outgrowth and that it is expressed by neurons, satellite cells and Schwmann cells.
laminin B1 chain is localized in satellite and glial cells of the dorsal root ganglia, and that the laminin B1 and B2 chains are expressed in neurons.

1) B2 and B1 laminin chain mRNAs are expressed in neurons, Schwann cells and satellite cells of adult DRG, 2) Merosin M chain mRNA is expressed in Schwann cells and to a lesser extent in satellite cells, and 3) A chain mRNA is not expressed by any cell type in the adult DRG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression and function of laminin in dorsal root ganglia (DRG).
the role of laminin and other extracellular matrix molecules in peripheral nerve regeneration.
the expression of laminin in the peripheral nervous system, particularly the DRG.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
laminin is a complex molecule that is synthesized by several different cell types in the DRG and that its expression is developmentally regulated.
laminin gene expression is not restricted to the Schwann cells, and that the neuronal laminin gene expression pattern is not identical to that of nonneuronal elements.
laminin is a heteropolymeric glycoprotein composed of three nonidentical polypeptide chains designated A, B, and M, and that the A chain is not expressed in the dorsal root ganglion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
laminin is a complex protein with multiple functional domains.
laminin is a substrate that can be used by neurons for axonal outgrowth.
laminin is expressed by both neuronal and nonneuronal cell types within the DRG, but the expression pattern is not uniform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B1 chain is expressed in a subpopulation of small neurons, and that the B2 chain is expressed in all neurons.
the laminin gene family is expressed in a complex and cell-type specific manner.

the expression of the laminin B2 chain by neurons and satellite cells suggests the possibility that laminin may play an important autocrine role in neuronal and nonneuronal interactions in DRG, in addition to its well-known role as an extracellular matrix component.
